chapters.title: The Studio Throne
chapters.body:
For eleven centuries, Vex ruled the Obsidian Dominion from a throne of black glass. Then came a small administrative misunderstanding, a portal, and a studio apartment on the fourth floor of a building with no elevator.

His new throne was a futon. His new dominion was three hundred square feet, one window, and a kitchenette he refused to call a kitchen.

"Very well," Vex declared to no one. "Every empire begins somewhere."

He wrote his first quest on a sticky note and placed it on the refrigerator with tremendous ceremony: QUEST: Purify the Mountain of Laundry.

The mountain was real. It occupied an entire corner. It had, Vex suspected, developed its own weather.

He approached it the way he had once approached fortresses: one section at a time. Darks. Lights. The mysterious category of items that were neither. Three loads later, the corner was visible again, and the futon smelled of something called Spring Meadow.

He drew a line through the sticky note and wrote beneath it: QUEST COMPLETE. +40 discipline. +12 clean socks. -1 afternoon.

Then he lay down on the futon throne and declared a rest period, which, in his dominion, was tradition.

chapters.title: The Guardian of the Bagging Area
chapters.body:
QUEST: Acquire seven days of provisions.

Vex entered the grocery store as a conqueror enters a new realm: slowly, with a cart, reading every sign aloud. The cereal aisle alone offered more choices than his former war council.

He chose his provisions with care. Bread. Eggs. Rice. A box of tea labeled Calm, which he regarded with suspicion and bought anyway.

Then he reached the self-checkout.

"UNEXPECTED ITEM IN THE BAGGING AREA," said the machine.

Vex had faced dragons. He had out-argued liches. He had never faced a guardian this persistent. Every item he placed, it asked him to place again. Each scan became a ritual: beep, wait, apologize to the machine for no reason.

A staff member eventually arrived, tapped the screen twice, and walked away without a word. Vex was deeply impressed.

At home, while he unpacked, he noticed a gray cat sitting on his windowsill, watching him. It had not been summoned. It had simply arrived, as familiars do.

He offered it a crust of bread. It rejected the offering, then sat on his quest log.

"Fine," said Vex. "You may stay. But you will be listed as a party member."

chapters.title: Party of Two
chapters.body:
One Saturday, Mrs. Pell from across the hall knocked with a request: could he help carry a bookshelf up the stairs?

Vex considered this. It was not on his quest log. It offered no loot. But a side quest, he knew from long experience, is where the best stories hide.

"I accept," he said, with a bow so deep that Mrs. Pell took a step back.

The bookshelf was heavy, the stairs were narrow, and the third-floor landing required a maneuver Vex called a tactical rotation. Mrs. Pell called it tilting it. They got it into her apartment without a single scratch on the wall.

She gave him a slice of lemon cake as a reward. Vex had once been paid in kingdoms. The cake was better.

Back home, the gray cat, now officially named Lieutenant Whiskers, was asleep on the futon throne. Vex did not have the heart to move it, so he sat on the floor beside it and looked at the sticky notes on the refrigerator. Laundry. Provisions. Bookshelf. Small quests, all cleared.

A dominion, he realized, is not land. It is a list of things you took care of.

He added one more sticky note: QUEST: Rest. Reward: unknown. Then he closed his eyes.
